This tests whether the CHANGE itself clusters spatially, not just the raw level in either period.

If you test statistical significance via a permutation/randomization test, use at least 500 random shuffles -- fewer permutations can produce an unstable p-value that lands on the wrong side of the 0.05 threshold just by chance, especially when the true effect is only moderate.

Thought: Compute global Moran's I on the NO₂ change values and assess significance via 999 permutations. Action:
```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Load data
df = pd.read_csv("chunks_csv/changespillover/changespillover_no2crime_no2_Q1_2023_to_Q2_2023.csv")
df['delta'] = df['Q2_2023_value'] - df['Q1_2023_value']
df_valid = df.dropna(subset=['delta']).reset_index(drop=True)

# Map boroughs to indices
boroughs = df_valid['borough'].tolist()
index = {b: i for i, b in enumerate(boroughs)}
n = len(boroughs)

# Load adjacency and filter to valid boroughs
adj = pd.read_csv(ADJACENCY_PATH)
adj = adj[adj['borough'].isin(boroughs) & adj['neighbor'].isin(boroughs)]

# Build weight matrix W
W = np.zeros((n, n))
for _, row in adj.iterrows():
    i = index[row['borough']]
    j = index[row['neighbor']]
    W[i, j] = 1
# S0
S0 = W.sum()

# Observed I
x = df_valid['delta'].values
xbar = x.mean()
d = x - xbar
num = d @ W @ d
den = (d * d).sum()
I_obs = (n / S0) * (num / den)

# Permutation test
perm_I = []
rng = np.random.default_rng()
for _ in range(999):
    perm = rng.permutation(x)
    pbar = perm.mean()
    dp = perm - pbar
    num_p = dp @ W @ dp
    den_p = (dp * dp).sum()
    I_p = (n / S0) * (num_p / den_p)
    perm_I.append(I_p)
perm_I = np.array(perm_I)

# p-value for positive autocorrelation
p_val = (np.sum(perm_I >= I_obs) + 1) / (len(perm_I) + 1)

print("I_obs:", I_obs)
print("p-value:", p_val)
```

p-value: 0.017
